no customer_id; use account_id; set campaign_id from ad_id (as text), date_day from date; include impressions, inline_link_clicks as clicks, spend as cost; set conversions to 0. - For each touchpoint: - customer_identifier uses customer_id when available; otherwise account_id as text; otherwise the string ''UNKNOWN_'' followed by campaign_id. - revenue per touchpoint uses conversions_value when present; otherwise revenue_30d; otherwise 0. - interaction_type is ''CONVERTING_CLICK'' when both clicks and conversions are positive; ''NON_CONVERTING_CLICK'' when clicks are positive only; ''IMPRESSION_ONLY'' when impressions are positive only; otherwise ''OTHER''. - Aggregate per customer_identifier into customer_segments: - active_days is the count of unique interaction dates; platforms_used is the count of unique platforms; campaigns_interacted is the count of unique campaigns. - total_impressions, total_clicks, total_cost, total_conversions, and total_revenue are sums over touchpoints (adding only non-null values). - first_interaction_date is the earliest interaction date; last_interaction_date is the latest; customer_lifespan_days is the number of days between them. - click_to_conversion_rate is conversions divided by clicks, scaled by 100 and rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when clicks are missing or not positive. - impression_to_click_rate is clicks divided by impressions, scaled by 100 and rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 when impressions are missing or not positive. - average_order_value is revenue divided by conversions, rounded to 2 decimals; returns 0 when conversions are missing or not positive. - customer_roas is revenue divided by cost, rounded to 4 decimals; returns 0 when cost is missing or not positive. - Final output per customer_identifier: - acquisition_cohort is the month of first_interaction_date; days_since_acquisition is the days from first_interaction_date to today. - customer_value_tier by total_revenue: >=1000 HIGH_VALUE; else if active_days>=2 then LIGHTLY_ENGAGED; else SINGLE_INTERACTION. - conversion_behavior by total_conversions: >=5 FREQUENT_CONVERTER; >=2 REPEAT_CONVERTER; =1 SINGLE_CONVERTER; else NON_CONVERTER. - recency_status by days since last_interaction_date: <=7 RECENT; <=30 MODERATE; <=90 DORMANT; else INACTIVE. - total_cost_attributed equals total_cost; all attribution revenue fields equal total_revenue. - Cohort placeholders: cohort_size=100; retained_month_1=85; retained_month_2=72; retained_month_3=63; retention_rate_month_1=85.0; retention_rate_month_2=72.0; retention_rate_month_3=63.0. - analysis_generated_at is the run timestamp with timezone. - Filter: keep customers with first_interaction_date in the last 12 months; order by total_revenue descending, then customer_identifier ascending. - Determinism and null policy: - Per-touchpoint revenue is never null due to fallback; sums add non-null values and yield null only if all inputs are null. - Percentage rates are on a 0–100 scale, rounded as stated, and default to 0 when the denominator is missing or not positive. - Distinct counts exclude nulls and do not count duplicates.'

For trend math, compute days since 1970‑01‑01 as a whole‑day index. - Rolling metrics are computed per platform ordered by date_day and include the current day; if fewer than N days exist, use the available days: - Moving averages: last 7 days (spend, ctr, cpc), last 30 days (spend, ctr, cpc), and last 90 days (spend). - spend_ewma is approximated as the same 7‑day simple average of spend. - Volatility: sample standard deviation over the last 30 days for ctr and cpc. - Trend and seasonality: - 90‑day rolling linear trend slopes for spend and ctr using the day index (days since epoch). - Prior‑period references: values from 365, 30, and 7 days earlier for YoY, MoM, and WoW comparisons. - Baselines: average ctr and spend by day_of_week, and by month_of_year, over the available 18‑month input window. - Anomalies and momentum: - Percent change vs prior periods is computed when the prior value is >0; otherwise NULL. - z‑scores are absolute deviations from the 30‑day mean scaled by the 30‑day standard deviation; 0 when the standard deviation is not positive. - Day‑of‑week deviation is the absolute percent difference from the day‑of‑week average; NULL when the baseline is zero. - Momentum: spend is ACCELERATING when the 7‑day average exceeds 110% of the 30‑day average, DECELERATING when below 90%, else STABLE; ctr is IMPROVING when the 7‑day average exceeds 105% of the 30‑day average, DECLINING when below 95%, else STABLE. - Trend direction from the 90‑day spend slope: STRONG_UPTREND (>0.1), MILD_UPTREND (>0 to 0.1], STRONG_DOWNTREND (<-0.1), MILD_DOWNTREND (<0 to -0.1], else SIDEWAYS. - Forecasting and confidence: - 30‑day trend forecasts add 30 times the 90‑day slope to the 30‑day average (for spend and ctr). - Seasonal factors are ratios of the daily values to the corresponding monthly averages; else VOLATILE when WoW spend change is >50% or <‑50%; else OPTIMIZING when ctr momentum is IMPROVING and spend momentum is STABLE; else SCALING when spend momentum is ACCELERATING and ctr momentum is STABLE; contract_evidence.quote: business_logic: '- Executive KPIs (last 12 months): For each platform and month, compute monthly investment (sum of spend), average daily spend, active days, totals for impressions/clicks/conversions/revenue, average CTR/CPC/CPA/ROAS (CTR and ROAS rounded to 4 decimals; CPC and CPA to 2), and volatility as the standard deviation of daily CTR (rounded to 4) and CPC (rounded to 2). Growth and anomaly placeholders are set to zero. - Customer insights (last 12 months): For each acquisition cohort month, compute new customers (distinct count), cohort revenue (sum), average customer value and lifespan, counts of high-value, highly engaged, and frequent converters, average retention for months 1–3, average customer ROAS and order value, average platforms used per customer, and count of multi-platform customers (used more than one platform). - Geographic performance (last 6 months): For each month and region, compute active countries (distinct count), regional investment (sum), average market CTR and CPC, spend in high-opportunity markets (sum) and count of such markets, mature market ratio (share of markets classified as mature), average market share and performance percentiles, and average multi-channel adoption. - Unified performance (last 12 months): For each month, compute active platforms (distinct count), monthly totals for impressions/clicks/spend/conversions/revenue, blended averages for CTR/CPC/ROAS (rounded as above), variance across platforms for CTR (rounded to 4) and CPC (rounded to 2), designate platform leaders (CTR leader is google_ads; efficiency and ROAS leaders are amazon_ads), and campaign metrics (distinct active campaigns, average campaign age, counts of new vs established campaigns). - Strategic insights by month: - Investment efficiency grade from overall ROAS thresholds (≥3.0, ≥2.0, ≥1.0, else). - Month-over-month growth rate as percent change in monthly spend versus the prior month, rounded to 2, and set to NULL if no prior month exists. - Portfolio diversification based on active platforms and CTR variance. - Expansion mode based on the ratio of new to established campaigns. - Performance consistency based on CTR and CPC variance thresholds. - Carry forward monthly totals, blended metrics, counts, and platform leaders. - Final output: Start from strategic insights; left join platform-level KPIs by month; left join cohort-level customer insights by cohort month; left join regional geographic performance by month; filter to the last 6 reporting months; group by month and the exposed categorical fields. - Aggregate per reporting_month: customer and geographic metrics are averaged or summed across joined rows; leader platform KPIs are taken from the platform that matches the designated leader; anomaly days use the maximum; performance volatility uses the average; platform growth uses the average; scaling and optimizing days use sums. - Recommendations and strategies: - Executive recommendation based on efficiency grade, consistency, expansion status, growth rate, and overall ROAS (with a default fallback). - Allocation strategy prioritizes when efficiency and ROAS leaders align; else considers low overall ROAS; else considers high average spend in high-opportunity markets; else defaults. Comparisons against aggregated values treat NULLs as not satisfying thresholds. - Customer strategy insight evaluates retention, high-value customer mix (with zero-division protection), and cross-platform engagement, with a default fallback. - Data quality and metadata: platforms_with_data is the count of platforms present in the platform KPI join for the month (0 when none); analysis_period_start and analysis_period_end both equal the reporting_month; dashboard_generated_at is the current timestamp; results are ordered by reporting_month descending.'

contract_evidence.quote: business_logic: '- Build the baseline from unified campaign metrics limited to the last 12 months. - Group by platform and the calendar month of date_day; compute monthly totals (spend, impressions, clicks, conversions, 30-day revenue) and monthly averages (CTR rounded to 4 decimals, CPC rounded to 2, ROAS rounded to 4); all aggregations ignore NULLs. - Count distinct campaigns: active (all), new (lifecycle LAUNCH), and established (lifecycle ESTABLISHED); NULL campaign IDs are excluded. - Compute volatility as the standard deviation of CTR and CPC within each platform-month; if fewer than two non-NULL observations, volatility is NULL. - Per platform, order months chronologically to derive: - Month-over-month spend growth: percent change from the prior month (rounded to 2 decimals); if the prior value is not positive, set to 0. - Month-over-month CTR change: percent change from the prior month (rounded to 2 decimals); if the prior value is not positive, set to 0. - 3-month rolling averages for spend, CTR, and ROAS using the current month and two preceding months. - Spend momentum: ACCELERATING if current spend is >10% above prior month, DECELERATING if >10% below, otherwise STABLE; if no prior month, STABLE. - CTR momentum: IMPROVING if current CTR is >5% above prior month, DECLINING if >5% below, otherwise STABLE; if no prior month, STABLE. - Predictions: - Next-month spend: 3-month spend average scaled by 1.15 when accelerating, 0.85 when decelerating, otherwise unchanged. - Next-month CTR: 3-month CTR average scaled by 1.10 when improving, 0.90 when declining, otherwise unchanged. - Risk level: HIGH_RISK when CTR volatility > 0.5 and MoM spend growth > 50%; MEDIUM_RISK when CTR volatility > 0.3 or absolute MoM spend growth > 25%; otherwise LOW_RISK. - Anomaly probability: 35 when CTR volatility > 1.0 or CPC volatility > 2.0; 20 when CTR volatility > 0.5 or CPC volatility > 1.0; 25 when absolute MoM spend growth > 50%; otherwise 10. - Confidence: HIGH_CONFIDENCE when absolute MoM spend growth < 10% and CTR volatility < 0.3; MEDIUM_CONFIDENCE when absolute MoM spend growth < 25% and CTR volatility < 0.5; otherwise LOW_CONFIDENCE. - Final output per platform-month: - Baselines: current_monthly_spend, current_avg_ctr, current_avg_cpc, current_avg_roas from the monthly aggregates. - Budget recommendation: increase if accelerating and ROAS ≥ 2.0; decrease if decelerating or ROAS < 1.0; otherwise maintain. - Predicted ROAS: +10% when ROAS ≥ 2.5 and CTR momentum improving; −10% when ROAS < 1.5 and CTR momentum declining; otherwise unchanged. - Risk mitigation and strategic recommendation are set to the exact strings defined by the CASE rules. - Revenue scenarios: expected revenue at current ROAS = predicted spend × current avg ROAS; optimized = predicted spend × predicted ROAS; incremental = predicted spend × (predicted ROAS − current avg ROAS). - Success probability: VERY_HIGH when confidence is HIGH and risk is LOW; HIGH when confidence is HIGH/MEDIUM and risk is not HIGH; MEDIUM when confidence is MEDIUM; otherwise LOW. - Metadata: generated timestamp at query run, base date is today, target date is 30 days after the base date. - Filter to months within the last six months; results are ordered by platform ascending and performance month descending.'
